summary: A guide to preparing homes and businesses for internet outages, prompted by a record number of interruptions reported since September 1, 2023. It draws on named experts and case examples to recommend backup connectivity, offline access, non-digital records, UPS units, response plans, security precautions, insurance, and regular plan reviews. It closes by advising patience and flexibility during outages.
one_line: Practical tips, with expert quotes and examples, for homes and businesses to prepare for and cope with internet outages.
key_facts: A record number of internet interruptions have been reported since September 1, 2023.
Virtual Solutions, a remote consultancy headed by Rajesh Singh, can lose significant revenue from an hour without connectivity.
Sarah Gibson, a home-based graphic designer, relied on a portable hotspot on October 15, 2023, when her primary connection failed during a project deadline.
David Lopez of FinTech Innovations suggests cloud services with offline modes, such as Google Drive and Dropbox, which let users save documents locally.
Jenna Matthews, a local baker, kept operating during the several-hour internet outage on November 7, 2023, thanks to her order book and supplier contact list.
Lawrence Kim recommends mobile data plans that include tethering or hotspot use, while warning that mobile data can get expensive if used extensively.
Several Nashville neighborhoods had power outages on October 29, 2023, a case for using a UPS to keep modems and routers running.
Edward Chan, owner of a small logistics company, stresses having a phone tree to notify employees and clients of internet issues.
Thompson's Legal Consultancy responded rapidly to the December 3, 2023 service breakdown because of meticulous preemptive planning.
Cybersecurity expert Aisha Gupta warns that cyber threats can escalate during outages; devices need up-to-date antivirus and public Wi-Fi should be avoided for business.
Mike Donovan of Secure Business Insurance advises businesses to consider insurance covering losses from service interruptions.
Christina Yang of Retail Sphere recommends annual reviews of contingency plans.
Derek Frost of SwiftConnect says customers who proactively engage with their ISPs typically experience less downtime and get more accurate restoration information.
Monitoring services can notify you the moment an outage occurs, even when you are not on-site.
